author: Victor Dergunov
title: Source: Quartz.com Why Apple Will Retain Its Trillion Doll
text:
Source: Quartz.com 

Why Apple Will Retain Its Trillion Dollar Trajectory 

Well, it’s official Apple ( AAPL ) is now oversold. The world’s most valuable public company has declined by nearly 10% over the past 2 weeks, the slide has erased roughly $80 billion worth of value from its market cap. To make matters even more perplexing, the steep decline in Apple shares comes just weeks and days prior to the company’s February 1 st 2018 Q1 earnings announcement. Which is projected to be the company’s most successful financial period in history, delivering more than $80 billion in revenues. Naturally, some logical questions arise, like is this selloff justified? Is this all-mighty tech giant going to shed more of its market value following the earnings report? Or is this an additional buying opportunity amid the company’s path towards its trillion-dollar future? 

iPhone X Sales Concerns 

It’s been widely reported that Apple is slashing iPhone X January – March period production from 40 million units down to just 20 million, due to slower than expected sales in Europe, the U.S., and China. It appears that Apple expected consumers to be more enthusiastic about forking out $999 and more per iPhone. However, it seems that many customers are more inclined to stick with Apple’s older design and an older price tag for that matter. Although this may appear as discouraging news at first sight, there are several elements investors should consider. 

iPhone Facts 

First, it is important to mention that the iPhone X is still in the somewhat experimental stage of its existence, and has not yet become broadly entrenched in popular culture or widely adopted. The fact is that many iPhone users still prefer the older version of the iPhone. The current design has become a kind of culture symbol and is entrenched in the hearts and minds’ of many consumers. Moreover, it is priced more competitively, therefore making it an obvious choice for many iPhone users. 

Second, this is the widest selection of iPhones Apple has ever had. In addition to the X, Apple also has the iPhone 8, 8 Plus, 7, 7 Plus, 6, 6 Plus, as well as the SE. Essentially Apple is offering consumers 8 different iPhone models, so, naturally some cannibalization is going to occur. The important element is that an increasing lineup of phones should allow Apple to capture additional market share in the overall smartphone market

Source: Phonearena.com 

iPhone sales have been gaining significant market share in many areas recently. In 2017, yoy iPhone sales were up by 4.7% in the U.S. to 34%, in Japan iPhone sales were up by a remarkable 7.8% to 48.4%, in Australia sales rose by 5.6%, in Spain by 1.5%, in Italy by 1.3%, and in Germany by 0.5%. The only modestly significant decline appears to be in France with a yoy decline of 2.7%. Apple should continue to increase its market share, and the introduction of the iPhone X should help Apple in the long run, not hurt the company’s growth potential, even if the X is not a blowout blockbuster right away.

Source: 9to5mac.com
